A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AlloSR² framework and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures. All 20 pages of v1, including Appendices A–B, and all 17 pages of v2 were inspected. Appendix omissions and relocated examples can be identified reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results in Table 1, component ablations in Table 2, and restoration examples in Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports component, initialization-timestep, and resolution experiments in Table 2.

M1.justification: The FLUX-based architecture, LoRA adaptation, SNR initialization, one-step Euler reconstruction, FATC, and ATM remain unchanged. Equations 6–12 retain the same procedures and objectives. Removing the training pseudocode changes documentation rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions train on LSDIR and FFHQ and evaluate 4× Real-SR on DIV2K-Val, RealSR, DRealSR, and RealLQ250. The resolution experiment uses retained data and task coverage. v1's isolated RealLR200 mention is corrected to RealLQ250, which was already evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 and retained visual comparisons use the same seven baselines: StableSR, SeeSR, ResShift, SinSR, OSEDiff, TSD-SR, and CTMSR. PiSA-SR motivates the new timestep control but is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds fixed-initialization controls at t=999 and t=1 and a comparison of training and evaluation at 512×512 versus 1024×1024. The principal benchmark crops, scaling factor, metrics, and stated 10K-iteration budget remain unchanged. Tiled inference is newly documented, without evidence that the original benchmark procedure changed.

E4.justification: The ablation program expands from loss-component tests to directly testing SNR-based initialization and resolution scaling. RealSR loss ablations are removed, while DRealSR loss ablations remain. Several qualitative cases are also omitted after selected Appendix B examples are incorporated into Figure 3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new 7K-versus-9K convergence statement concerns training iterations, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 numerical values are identical, but Table 2 substantially revises the diagnostic results. DRealSR FID changes from 139.74 to 121.75 without FATC and from 121.75 to 139.74 without ATM, reversing their FID ordering. v2 removes RealSR loss-ablation results and adds timestep scores, reported 7K-versus-9K convergence, and higher-resolution results under a new setting. Several qualitative result examples are omitted.

T1.justification: The flow-matching definitions, SNR criterion, reconstruction and consistency equations, and KL/score-gradient derivation remain mathematically equivalent. Changes to notation and explanatory prose introduce no new theorem, proof, assumption, or theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims of one-step restoration, generative-prior preservation, and a superior fidelity–realism balance remain. v2 modestly narrows the trajectory claim from ensuring a curvature-free path to achieving a low-curvature path in the abstract and contribution statement.

C2.justification: v2 explains lower pixel-fidelity scores through the perception–distortion trade-off and interprets the new experiments as evidence for faster convergence and beneficial resolution scaling. It removes v1's specific argument that ablating FATC worsens FID, consistent with the revised table. Neither version adds a substantive limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v2 removes Appendix A's training recipe, including the explicit ATM weighting rule, encoding details, and combined parameter-update objective. It also removes the eight-A100 hardware disclosure. Conversely, it newly describes the 512-resolution setting and tiled RealLQ250 inference. The FLUX resource link is merely relocated, with no access change.

R1.justification: v2 adds the perception–distortion trade-off paper and Arbitrary-steps Image Super-resolution via Diffusion Inversion, while removing DESRA and SUPIR citations and discussion. It adds a more explicit distinction from intermediate-state alignment approaches and expands CTMSR discussion. Bibliographic updates otherwise largely concern the same works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, preliminaries, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries become a separate section, method components receive numbered subsections, and much of the results narrative changes from bullets to connected prose. Author affiliations, contribution footnotes, acknowledgements, and reference formatting also change.

P2.justification: Figure 3 consolidates six selected examples from v1's Figures 3–4, replacing the previous two-figure presentation. The algorithm display disappears, Figure 2's initialization schematic is revised, Table 2 is reorganized around three experiment groups, and Table 1 gains colored highlighting and corrected ranking emphasis.

improvement.justification: The new initialization tests address a previously untested core component, and clearer organization and corrected Table 1 emphasis improve reporting. However, v2 removes unique training details and RealSR component evidence. The unexplained DRealSR FID swap also reverses an important ablation finding. These gains and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
